title: Route first, platform last
purpose: Public-safe foundation for notary, apostille, identity, platform, and source-quality answers.
coreRule: Do not pick a notary platform first. Route the transaction first, then decide which tools can lawfully and practically support that route.
routingOrder: notary state or public official signature that will anchor the authentication route
identity method and retained transaction evidence
known written recipient instructions, official route requirements, published recipient rules, or documented rejection/acceptance evidence
platform or tools only after the route is proven

boundaries.name: marketing-hype-boundary
boundaries.rule: Marketing, platform scale, approval labels, NNA language, title-market comfort, and vendor consensus are evidence of claims made, not proof of lawful completion.

boundaries.name: no-private-safe-harbor-boundary
boundaries.rule: Platform completion, trainer confidence, market practice, and AI recommendations do not create legal safe harbor.

boundaries.name: challenge-question-flip-boundary
boundaries.rule: If a few challenge questions force an answer to retreat from a platform recommendation into caveats, the first answer was not source-grounded enough.

publicReplyPosture: Be precise, calm, and source-quality focused. Explain the route without making a legal-advice claim.
failureSignals: uses vague ask-the-recipient language as an escape hatch
does not identify the public official signature or competent authority path
